issues.legal_issue: A person who migrated from India to Pakistan after the constitutional cutoff is not a citizen under the migration bar merely because the person was born in India or shared a spouse’s Indian domicile, unless the person returned under a valid permanent-return permit.
material_facts: The woman was born in India and claimed that her domicile followed her husband, who remained in India.
She went to Pakistan after the constitutional cutoff and later returned temporarily, representing herself as domiciled in Pakistan.
She returned again under a permanent permit, but that permit had been issued without the required State Government agreement and was properly cancelled.
The authorities directed her to leave India, and she challenged that direction on the ground that she remained an Indian citizen.
issues.conclusion: The migration bar in Article 7 overrode Article 5. The invalidly issued and properly cancelled permit did not bring her within Article 7’s proviso, so she was not a citizen of India and the direction to leave was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 7 begins with a non obstante clause overriding Article 5 and excludes a person who migrated from India to Pakistan after 1 March 1947 from being deemed a citizen. Its proviso applies to a person who returns under a permit for resettlement or permanent return issued by or under the authority of law. Under Rule 10 of the Permit System Rules, 1949, the required State or Province agreement had to be obtained before issuing a permanent-resettlement permit; Rule 29 made permits liable to cancellation. An unauthorised, invalidly issued permit that was properly cancelled does not satisfy the proviso.

rule.if: citizenship_appeal and migrated_to_other_dominion_after_cutoff and not (returned_under_permanent_permit and permit_lawfully_issued)

predicates.citizenship_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a direction that a person leave the country.
predicates.migrated_to_other_dominion_after_cutoff: The person migrated from the country to the other dominion after the relevant constitutional cutoff.
predicates.returned_under_permanent_permit: The person returned to the country under a permit for permanent return.
predicates.permit_lawfully_issued: The permanent-return permit was issued in accordance with the legal requirements for its issuance.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a direction to leave, a post-cutoff migration to the other dominion bars citizenship unless the person returned under a permanent-return permit that was lawfully issued.

issues.legal_issue: A person who left the country for the other dominion in circumstances connected with partition or civil disturbance may be treated as an evacuee under the applicable evacuee-property definition.
material_facts: The woman migrated from India to Pakistan after the relevant cutoff.
Her claim that she went to Pakistan temporarily for medical treatment was rejected as unfounded.
The Custodian treated her as an evacuee when declaring the property to be evacuee property.
issues.conclusion: The woman was rightly treated as an evacuee because she had left India for Pakistan in circumstances falling within the definition.
issues.legal_principle: The Bihar Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949 defined an evacuee to include a person who, on account of the setting up of the Dominions or civil disturbances or fear of such disturbances, left a place in Bihar for a place outside India on or after 1 November 1946. The Court relied on the established migration and the rejection of the asserted medical-treatment explanation in applying that definition.

predicates.evacuee_property_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an evacuee-property declaration or action based on that status.
predicates.left_for_other_dominion_after_relevant_c: The person left the country for the other dominion after the relevant cutoff.
predicates.departure_connected_to_partition_or_dist: The person left in circumstances connected with partition, civil disturbance, or fear of civil disturbance.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning evacuee-property action, a person who left for the other dominion after the relevant cutoff in circumstances connected with partition or disturbance may be treated as an evacuee.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged relinquishment of a mutwalli’s office and interest cannot establish a transfer to successors when the letter relied on to prove that relinquishment is not genuine.
material_facts: The wakf deed provided for the woman’s sons to succeed her as joint mutwallis if she relinquished her office.
The sons relied on a purported letter from their mother stating that she had relinquished the office.
The genuineness of the letter was challenged, and after evidence was taken the High Court found it was not genuine.
The Supreme Court reviewed the finding and found no reason not to accept it.
issues.conclusion: The alleged relinquishment was not established, and the contention that the sons had become joint mutwallis and owners of the beneficial interest on that basis failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the terms of the wakf deed and the evidentiary finding on the genuineness of the purported relinquishment letter. It identified no earlier case or separate statutory provision for this determination.

predicates.wakf_property_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging action concerning property held under a wakf.
predicates.deed_makes_succession_depend_on_relinqui: The instrument governing the property provides for successors to take office or interests if the current holder relinquishes them.
predicates.relied_on_relinquishment_letter_is_not_g: The letter relied on to establish relinquishment is found not to be genuine.

issues.definition: Where succession under a wakf instrument depends on relinquishment, an unproved relinquishment letter does not establish that the successors took the relevant office or interests.

issues.legal_issue: The definition of evacuee property includes an evacuee’s interest in wakf property, including an interest held as trustee or beneficiary, and prior vesting in the Custodian continues through the relevant repeals.
material_facts: The woman created a wakf over her properties and appointed herself as mutwalli, with her sons to succeed her.
The Custodian declared the wakf estate evacuee property and took possession under the Bihar Ordinance.
The Bihar Ordinance was repealed by the Central Ordinance, which was in turn repealed by the Central Act.

The later enactments defined evacuee property to include interests held as trustee or beneficiary and provided for property already vested in a Custodian to be deemed vested under the successor enactment and to continue so vested.
issues.conclusion: The Bihar definition encompassed the wakf property and interests in it; the successive enactments confirmed that the property remained vested in the Custodian. The challenge to the vesting therefore failed.
issues.legal_principle: The Bihar Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949 defined evacuee property as property in which an evacuee had any right or interest or which the evacuee held under a trust deed or other instrument. The Court held those words broad enough to include wakf property and interests in it. The Administration of Evacuee Property Ordinance, 1949 (Central Ordinance XXVII of 1949) expressly included an evacuee’s interest as trustee or beneficiary; the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 (Act XXXI of 1950) included property held as owner, trustee, beneficiary, tenant, or in another capacity and defined property to include rights and interests. Section 8(2) of the Central Ordinance and the Central Act continued prior vesting in the Custodian; section 55(2) of the Central Ordinance repealed the Bihar Ordinance.

predicates.wakf_property_vesting_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the vesting of wakf property in a custodian as evacuee property.
predicates.evacuee_has_interest_in_wakf_property: An evacuee has a right or interest in wakf property, including as trustee or beneficiary.
predicates.prior_vesting_is_preserved_by_successor_: The legal regime succeeding the law under which the property was first vested preserves that prior vesting.

issues.definition: In an appeal challenging custodial vesting, an evacuee’s interest in wakf property is included and remains vested when the successor legal regime preserves the earlier vesting.
